summary: Deployment-readiness check after quoting DATA_ENCRYPTION_KEY in backend/.env. Backend starts (supervisor RUNNING, no errors, 0 'decrypt failed' log lines). python-dotenv strips the quotes: loaded key is 44 chars, starts with '-', no quote chars, so it is the same Fernet key. All existing encrypted docs decrypt with it: measurements 8/8, weight_history 22/22, 0 plaintext docs left (no data loss). API: GET /api/ 200; GET /api/profile/measurements returns plaintext numbers; GET weight-history returns numeric weight_kg with no weight_enc in the response; PUT inseam_cm=75 then GET returns 75 and the mongo doc holds only 'enc'; POST auto-measure 200 with precision=98, method=auto_photo, brand_sizes present. Existing test_auto_measure_encryption.py suite: 11/11 pass. Frontend (owner gate set): /dashboard and /profile load with no page errors and no 4xx/5xx API calls; /profile shows the auto-measure-result panel (98% precision, 6 brands, estimated measurements) built from the saved data.
critical_code_review_comments: _dec() returns None on InvalidToken, and _get_measurements then returns {}. A wrong key would make data silently look empty instead of failing loudly. Consider a startup self-check that decrypts one known doc and refuses to start (or logs CRITICAL) on InvalidToken, so a bad key can't go unnoticed in production.
_set_measurements after a failed decrypt would overwrite the doc with only the new patch, which permanently loses the data if the key is ever wrong. Guard against writing when decrypt failed.
seed_data_creation: None. Test user fam_test_1791784817 left in the auto_photo state (inseam later overwritten by auto-measure to 74).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run test_encryption_key_env.py with '-n 0' (pytest.ini enables xdist). Running it in parallel with test_auto_measure_encryption.py races on the same user: test_put_measurements_still_works clears method/precision/brand_sizes by design. check_decrypt_all.py checks that every encrypted doc decrypts with the current .env key.
rca of the issue: Unquoted value starting with '-' could be misparsed by some deploy env loaders. Quoting keeps the value byte-identical under python-dotenv (verified), so no re-encryption was needed.
